Raymond III Count of Tripoli was one of the most powerful and influential noble leaders of the 12th century Crusader states in the Levant. His rule over the County of Tripoli spanned from 1152 until his death in 1187 and he held significant additional power through land holdings and political ties in the neighboring Kingdom of Jerusalem. He played a central role in nearly every major political and military event of the Crusader states during the decades leading up to the catastrophic 1187 Battle of Hattin that ended most independent Crusader control of the Holy Land.

The first core section of his Wikipedia biography is *Origins and Early Life*. Raymond was born around 1140 as the only son of Raymond II Count of Tripoli and Hodierna of Jerusalem who was herself a member of the ruling royal family of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. His father was assassinated by a group of Nizari Assassins in 1152 when Raymond was only twelve years old. The young noble was not yet old enough to rule in his own right so Baldwin III King of Jerusalem served as regent of Tripoli for three years until Raymond reached the age of majority in 1155. Shortly after taking power Raymond married Eschiva of Bures the widow of Walter of Saint Omer the Prince of Galilee. This marriage gave Raymond direct control over the large and wealthy Lordship of Galilee within the Kingdom of Jerusalem which doubled his total land holdings and made him one of the richest secular lords in the entire Levant. In 1164 Raymond joined a combined force of Crusader nobles to intervene in a succession dispute in the neighboring Muslim state of Aleppo. His army was defeated by the forces of Nur ad-Din the Zengid sultan of Syria at the Battle of Harim. Raymond was captured and held in prison in Aleppo for almost ten years until he was ransomed in 1173. He returned to Tripoli to resume his rule and immediately began working to strengthen his county’s defenses against further Muslim attacks.

A second key section of his life documented on the page is *Regency of the Kingdom of Jerusalem*. In 1185 the dying King Baldwin IV of Jerusalem who suffered from advanced leprosy named Raymond as regent for his young heir Baldwin V. Baldwin IV had chosen Raymond over other powerful nobles like Guy of Lusignan because Raymond was viewed as a more experienced and moderate leader who could unite the fractious Crusader nobility against the growing threat of the Ayyubid sultan Saladin. Raymond served as regent for two years and negotiated a truce with Saladin to give the Crusader states time to rebuild their depleted military forces. The truce was deeply unpopular with more hardline nobles and with powerful military orders like the Knights Templar who favored immediate open war with Saladin. When Baldwin V died in 1186 Raymond initially tried to claim the throne for himself or for an alternative adult candidate but was forced to concede to Guy of Lusignan after Guy secured the support of most of the military orders and the conservative noble factions of Jerusalem.

The final critical section of his biography is *Battle of Hattin and Death*. Tensions between Raymond and Guy remained high for months after Guy took the throne but Saladin’s large scale invasion of the Kingdom of Jerusalem in 1187 forced the two men to reconcile to face the common external enemy. Raymond led the vanguard of the combined Crusader army at the Battle of Hattin which ended in a total catastrophic defeat for the Crusader forces. Most of the Crusader leadership including Guy of Lusignan and the master of the Knights Templar was captured or killed in the battle but Raymond managed to escape with a small group of his personal retainers. He fled first to Tripoli to arrange defenses for his county and then to Tyre where he fell ill with pleurisy shortly after his arrival. He died in Tyre in September 1187 only a few months after the disastrous defeat at Hattin. His death and the widespread collapse of Crusader power across the Levant left the County of Tripoli heavily vulnerable to Ayyubid attack though the small state would survive for another century before falling to Mamluk forces in 1289.

Hark thou wanderer of western climes who seek’st the grace
Of Nippon’s isle where ancient joy and modern wonder brace
Thy seven day journey shall unfold as fair as any tale
Bards told in hall or hut when ale did make their tongues not fail
No woe shall cross thy path no ill shall mar thy stay
For Nippon’s gods do smile on those who come to praise her sway

First day thou shalt touch down in Edo’s misty bay
Where neon glow doth rival stars that light the milky way
Thou shalt repair to a ryokan of wood and rice straw mat
Where rest shall soothe thy limbs from travel’s weary fat
At eve thou shalt wander Shibuya’s teeming cross
Where throngs do move like tides that beat on ocean’s moss
Thou shalt gaze on Hachikō’s statue that standeth firm and true
A monument to faith that doth all time outdo
Thou shalt sup upon ramen rich with pork and savory broth
That warmeth thy cold bones and filleth thy heart with joy

Second day thou shalt rise with the sun’s first golden ray
To walk Asakusa’s lanes where ancient spirits play
Thou shalt pass through Kaminarimon’s gate where red lanterns hang
Like giant beating hearts that to the gods do sing
Thou shalt offer coin at Sensō-ji’s hallowed shrine
And whisper thy wish for joy to powers divine
Thou shalt snack on taiyaki filled with red bean sweet
That melteth on thy tongue and maketh thy day complete
At midday thou shalt ride the train to Kamakura’s shore
Where the great bronze Buddha doth sit forevermore
Thou shalt walk the sand where waves do kiss the ground
And hear the sea’s low song that doth all care confound
At eve thou shalt return to Edo’s bright embrace
To sup on sushi fresh from the bay’s cold blue space

Third day thou shalt board the shinkansen silver and fast
That flieth o’er the land like an arrow cast
Thou shalt gaze on rice fields green and villages small
That pass like fleeting dreams beneath thy gentle call
Ere noon thou shalt reach Kyoto’s ancient ground
Where temples cling to hills like jewels on a queen’s crown
Thou shalt first walk Fushimi Inari’s mountain path
Beneath ten thousand torii gates of crimson hue
Where light doth filter through in streaks of gold and red
And wind doth whisper tales of the long dead
Thou shalt leave an ema tablet carved with thy heart’s desire
At the shrine’s old altar where the sacred fires
Do burn both day and night for all who come to pray
At eve thou shalt wander Gion’s cobblestone way
Where geisha do glide like cherry blossoms on the breeze
Their obis tied tight their faces pale as winter snow
Thou shalt sup on kaiseki a feast of many a course
Each dish a work of art crafted with gentle force

Fourth day thou shalt rise at dawn’s first faint light
To see Kinkaku-ji shine on the lake’s still height
The Golden Pavilion doth glow like a sun fallen low
Its reflection in the water doth its own glory show
Thou shalt walk to Arashiyama’s bamboo grove so tall
Where stalks do reach the sky and rustle soft and low
Their sound like whispers of the spirits of the place
That doth all hurry and all worry erase
Thou shalt cross Togetsukyo Bridge that spans the river wide
Like a bow bent by a giant’s hand and tied
To the hills on either side that rise up to the sky
At midday thou shalt climb Iwatayama’s hill high
Where wild macaques do roam and take food from thy hand
Their eyes so wise their fur so soft and grand
At eve thou shalt attend a tea ceremony true
Where a master doth pour matcha green and new
Thou shalt learn the grace of quiet and of slow
That doth make the heart and soul both grow

Fifth day thou shalt travel to Nara’s ancient land
The cradle of Nippon’s faith so old and grand
Thou shalt walk Nara Park where deer do bow their heads
To beg for crackers from the hands of those who tread
Their grassy lanes and shaded paths so sweet
Thou shalt visit Tōdai-ji’s hall so vast and meet
The great bronze Buddha that doth sit so high
Beneath a roof that reacheth almost to the sky
Thou shalt squeeze through the pillar’s hole so narrow and so tight
That granteth enlightenment to all who pass through right
At midday thou shalt sup on persimmon leaf sushi sweet
That doth the taste of autumn’s fruit complete
Thou shalt wander Heijō Palace’s ruins old
Where emperors of old did rule their land of gold
At eve thou shalt return to Kyoto’s calm embrace
To walk the Philosopher’s Path where cherry blossoms grace
The canal that runneth slow and soft and clear
Thou shalt drink warm sake beneath the stars so near

Sixth day thou shalt travel to Osaka’s brash bright shore
Where joy and food and laughter do forever pour
Thou shalt climb Osaka Castle that standeth firm and high
Upon a hill of stone beneath the blue sky
Thou shalt learn the tale of Hideyoshi the warlord bold
Who built the castle bright his power to hold
Thou shalt wander Dotonbori’s lanes so loud and bright
Where the Glico Man doth glow with all his might
Thou shalt sup on takoyaki fried octopus balls so warm
That burst with flavor and do all care disarm
Thou shalt eat okonomiyaki the savory pancake grand
Filled with cabbage meat and sauce so sweet and grand
Thou shalt play pachinko in a parlor full of light
Where bells do ring and balls do clatter day and night
At eve thou shalt ride a ferry on the Yodo River wide
To see the city’s lights dance on the tide

Seventh day thou shalt rise with a heart both glad and sad
For thy journey’s end doth make thy spirit feel bad
Thou shalt walk Osaka’s morning market bright and early
To buy souvenirs of matcha silk and pottery
For thy loved ones back home who wait for thy return
Thou shalt board the plane that doth make the sky burn
With the glow of dawn as thou dost fly away
But thou shalt carry Nippon with thee every day
The taste of ramen and sushi the sound of bamboo’s sigh
The sight of geisha gliding the warmth of the sky
The faith of the temples the joy of the people true
All these shall dwell in thy heart forever new
Fare thee well wanderer thy journey hath been told
Thy memories of Nippon shall never grow old

i’m writing this because i know you’ll just scroll past the 17 vote reminders i sent you on instagram, and you muted the group chat when lila started ranting about city council last week. fair, honestly, that whole thing was annoying.
remember last month when we were sitting on your fire escape, eating cold pizza, and you were complaining that your landlord raised your rent $300 for no reason, and the bus that takes you to your barista shift only comes every 45 minutes now, and that the only dog park within 3 miles is always full of broken glass so you can’t bring moose there? all that stuff is on the ballot this year. not just the big presidential race everyone yells about, the tiny local stuff that actually makes your day suck or not.
i know you said voting feels like a waste of time, that none of the people running care about people like us, and i get that. i felt the same way after the last election, when that park funding we voted for got rerouted to some stupid corporate parking garage. but this time the rent stabilization measure is actually written by people who live here, not some rich developer, and the bus funding line is tied directly to the route you take every day, no weird loopholes. even the school board race is voting on whether to keep the free after school snack program that your little sister stays for every day, so she doesn’t have to walk home alone while you’re at work.
i’m not gonna lecture you, i promise. i just don’t want us to complain about all this stuff for another two years and not have even tried to fix it. here’s the plan: i’ll pick you up at 5:30 right when your shift ends, i’ll already have your favorite matcha latte (extra foam, no sugar, just how you like it) in the car, and we can stop at that tater tot cart by the library on the way to the polls. the polling place is the old elementary school we went to, the one with the dinosaur murals on the gym wall, you don’t even have to look up the address. they take your expired driver’s license or your work id, even the old library card you have stuck in your wallet next to that photo of moose as a puppy. you don’t have to fill out every single race if you don’t know who the people are, just pick the ones you care about and leave the rest blank, that’s totally allowed.
after we vote, we can go back to my place, steal my roommate’s frozen mozzarella sticks, and marathon that terrible vampire show you’ve been begging me to watch. no agenda, no talking about politics after we’re done, just hanging out like we always do.
you don’t have to do this alone, and it doesn’t have to be this big, stressful thing. even just showing up for the tiny stuff that affects us counts more than you think.
text me when you get this so i know you’re in.
p.s. i also bought that sour cherry sour candy you love that only sells at the gas station by my house. it’s in my pantry, waiting for you. no takebacks.
p.p.s. moose is allowed to come too, obviously. i bought him a peanut butter treat for being the best co-pilot.

Leo, 32, part-time elementary school librarian, woke up with a cramp in his shoulder and the faint tinny hum of menu music ringing in his ears, leftover, he assumed, from the 12 hours he’d sunk into his favorite cozy open-world sim the night before. He stumbled to the kitchen to make toast, burning the heel of sourdough he’d baked over the weekend, and when he yelped and shook his stinging fingertip, a floating teal pop-up hovered an inch above his skin, text crisp as 16-bit pixels: Minor Burn Status, Duration: 2 Hours, Remedy: Cold Water + Bandage. Stumbling to the bathroom mirror, he spotted a thin green bar floating above his reflection, labeled LVL 12: Librarian, 78/200 XP, next to a tiny heart icon ticking down from 92/100 as his fingertip throbbed. When he grabbed his backpack to head to work, a glowing gold exclamation mark pulsed on his front door, and a quest prompt loaded as his fingers brushed the doorknob: Daily Main Quest: Lead Storytime for 12 3rd Graders, Reward: +25 XP, +5 Community Rep, Rare Space Sticker Drop. He froze, because that was the exact main quest he’d selected for his custom librarian character last night, right before he’d passed out on his couch, half-empty citrus energy drink sweating on his controller.

At first, panic hit sharp enough to make his vision swim: he fumbled for his phone, scrolling for his best friend Javi’s contact—the one he’d had since high school, the one who’d helped him move into his tiny apartment three years prior—only to find it missing, replaced by a list of tagged NPCs he’d interacted with a hundred times on his screen. He skipped the library, veering west toward the pine tree line he’d always thought was just decorative map filler, and when he passed the community garden, a silver-haired old lady with a quest mark over her sunhat waved him over, pressing a sun-warmed heirloom tomato into his palm before he could say a word—another mod he’d coded himself, after his grandma died and he couldn’t bring himself to plant her favorite tomato seeds in his cramped IRL fire escape planter. He kept walking until the sidewalk ended, the pine needles fuzzing into the soft, grainy render fog he’d complained about a dozen times on the game’s subreddit, and then he heard it: a high, rumbly meow that made his chest ache so bad he had to stop breathing for a second. Mochi, the tabby cat he’d lost to kidney failure three years prior, the one he’d spent three weekends modding into the game with custom purr files and a habit of curling up on his character’s desk during storytime prep, trotted out of the fog and curled around his ankles, a tiny permanent heart icon floating above her head. Leo sank to the cool grass, scratching the spot behind her ear that she’d always loved, and for the first time in two years, he didn’t feel the heavy, hollow burnout that had followed him every waking hour IRL. He didn’t know if he’d ever get back, or if he even wanted to—there was a storytime to run later, a tomato to plant, and a cat that was finally home again.

I woke up with zero hip stiffness, no groggy sleep inertia, and none of the lower back ache that had plagued me since buying my fancy $1,200 memory foam mattress two years prior. Six months later, that memory foam mattress is collecting dust in my garage, and I sleep full-time in a hammock strung between two stands in my bedroom. Turns out, that random camping hack has science-backed benefits that blow traditional mattresses out of the water.

First and most transformative for me? Hammocks eliminate the pressure points that cause chronic sleep pain. A 2020 study from the University of Bern compared pressure distribution across mattresses and suspended hammocks, finding that hammocks reduce peak pressure on the hips and shoulders by nearly 70% for average-weight adults. Mattresses, even plush memory foam ones, create hard pressure spikes where your heaviest body parts sink into the surface, cutting off circulation and triggering inflammation overnight. For my partner, who has a mild herniated disc from a college sports injury, the switch was life-changing: he stopped taking 200mg of ibuprofen every night before bed within two weeks of swapping his mattress for a hammock. Unlike adjustable beds that cost thousands to get the right alignment, a properly hung hammock (strung loose enough to create a 30-degree recline, not pulled tight like a banana) naturally cradles the spine in its neutral S-curve, no fancy remotes required.

That gentle sway you associate with lazy afternoon naps? It’s not just cozy—it’s a proven sleep supercharger. The subtle movement activates the parasympathetic nervous system, lowering cortisol (the stress hormone) and calming racing thoughts before bed. Most hammocks are made of tightly woven, breathable nylon or polyester that doesn’t trap debris, and you can toss the entire thing in the washing machine on cold in 2 minutes, no heavy lifting required. For people with mild sleep apnea, the 30-degree recline of a properly hung hammock also opens up the airway, reducing snoring and nighttime breathing interruptions. A friend of mine who’s had mild apnea for years told me his partner stopped wearing earplugs to bed three weeks after he switched to a hammock.

Let’s not sleep on the practical benefits, either. A high-quality camping hammock plus a sturdy indoor stand costs around $250 total—less than a quarter of the cost of a mid-tier queen mattress, and a fraction of the price of a luxury adjustable bed. For renters in tiny studio apartments or digital nomads who move every few months, hammocks are unbeatable for space: I take mine down every weekend to turn my bedroom into a yoga studio, and it fits in a carry-on when I visit family out of state. No more paying movers to haul a 100-pound mattress up three flights of stairs.

Now, let’s bust the two most common myths about full-time hammock sleeping. First: you can only sleep on your back. False. As long as you hang your hammock loose enough to create that flat, 30-degree recline (not pulled tight so it curves into a U), you can side sleep, stomach sleep, even curl up with a pillow just like you would on a mattress. **Subject: Invitation to Cross-Functional Q3 User Experience Strategy Alignment Meeting | Mandatory for All Listed Participants**

Hi Product Management User Research Customer Support Engineering and Marketing Core Team Members

This email is your official invitation to a mandatory cross functional meeting focused on aligning our entire team on Q3 priorities for improving core platform user experience. We have spent the last six weeks compiling and analyzing a comprehensive set of qualitative and quantitative user data spanning support ticket trends in app feedback user testing sessions and retention metrics. This data has revealed clear patterns of user frustration that are directly impacting our retention upsell and revenue goals for the year. We are bringing together representatives from every user facing function to collaborate on solutions that will address these pain points and drive meaningful results for both our users and our business.

The meeting will take place on Tuesday August 15 2024 from 10 AM to 12 PM Central Time. It will be hosted in a hybrid format to accommodate all team members. In person attendees can join us in Conference Room B on the third floor of the downtown headquarters. Remote attendees can join via the Zoom link included at the bottom of this email. We have blocked a full two hours for this discussion to ensure we have enough time to review all key data collaborate on solution ideas and lock in clear action items before we leave.

Invited attendees include all lead product managers for core workflow tools all senior user research associates all customer support team leads all engineering squad leads for front end and back end platform development all marketing campaign managers focused on user retention and all department heads involved in product strategy. If you receive this email you are expected to attend or send a designated alternate from your team who can speak to your department’s priorities and constraints. We cannot move forward with aligned strategy without representation from every invited function.

To set context for our discussion we want to share a high level overview of the data that prompted this meeting. We saw an 18 percent drop in 30 day user retention for new sign ups who complete onboarding during Q2 of this year. We also saw a 22 percent rise in support tickets related to core workflow navigation errors over the same time period. We have heard firsthand from support teams that users are experiencing consistent confusion when trying to move between the project creation and team assignment dashboards. Many users report spending 10 minutes or more searching for basic features that are buried under multiple nested menu layers. Our user research team ran 32 one on one interviews with users across free tier pro and enterprise plans to dig deeper into these pain points. They mapped every reported frustration to specific stages of the user journey to identify common patterns across all user segments. Our data science team confirmed that these navigation pain points are directly correlated with lower feature adoption rates for our highest value paid tools. Users who report navigation confusion are 47 percent less likely to upgrade to a paid plan within their first 60 days on the platform.

We have structured a detailed agenda to keep our discussion focused and productive. The first 15 minutes will be a Welcome and Q2 User Pain Point Recap led by our Head of User Research. This section will include a walkthrough of the top 10 user pain points pulled from support tickets interview transcripts and in app feedback. We will also show short clips from recent user testing sessions to ground the group in real user perspectives. The next 25 minutes will be a Data Deep Dive led by our Lead Data Analyst. This section will cover a full breakdown of the retention drop by user segment a map of how pain points tie to projected revenue loss and an outline of how navigation issues impact upsell conversion rates. The next 30 minutes will be a Cross Functional Brainstorming Session. We will break into small diverse groups each group will include one product manager one user researcher one support lead one engineer and one marketing lead. Each group will develop three high level solution ideas for the top two priority pain points identified in our pre meeting survey. The next 25 minutes will be a Group Shareback and Prioritization exercise. Each group will present their ideas to the full group and we will rank all ideas based on expected user impact implementation effort and alignment with our 2024 business goals. The final 25 minutes will be dedicated to Next Steps and Action Item Assignments. We will lock in a clear timeline for prototype development assign owners for each workstream and confirm the date for our first follow up check in meeting.

To ensure we make the most of our time together we require all attendees to complete a short set of pre work tasks by 5 PM Central Time on Wednesday August 9 2024. First review the Q2 User Pain Point Summary document linked in the resources section of this email. This document includes all key metrics user quotes and journey maps we will reference during our discussion. Spend 10 minutes noting any observations or initial solution ideas you want to bring to the brainstorm. Second if you are a customer support lead come prepared to share one specific example of a user issue you resolved in the last month that relates to platform navigation confusion. Third if you are an engineering lead come prepared to note any existing technical constraints that might impact proposed solution ideas. Fourth complete the short pre meeting survey linked in the resources section to rank the pain points you believe are most critical to address first. The survey takes less than 5 minutes to complete and will help us structure the brainstorm to focus on areas the whole team sees as high priority.

We have also organized logistics to support both in person and remote attendees. For in person attendees coffee light snacks and water will be available in Conference Room B starting 15 minutes before the meeting start time. We will have printed copies of the pain point summary and agenda for anyone who prefers physical materials. We will also have whiteboards and sticky notes available for the brainstorming activity. For remote attendees we will send a calendar reminder with the Zoom link 24 hours and 1 hour before the meeting starts. Please keep your camera on if possible to encourage active participation during the brainstorm and breakout sessions. We will use the Zoom breakout room feature for the small group activity so make sure you have the latest version of Zoom installed to avoid access issues. We will also have a dedicated facilitator monitoring the Zoom chat to capture questions and input from remote attendees throughout the meeting.

This meeting is a critical opportunity for us to shift our focus from building new features to fixing the core usability issues that are driving users away. Our internal projections show that even small targeted improvements to platform navigation could increase 30 day retention by as much as 25 percent and lift annual recurring revenue by over 1.2 million dollars in the next 12 months. We intentionally included representatives from every department that touches the user experience to ensure we consider every perspective and build solutions that are feasible user friendly and aligned with our go to market strategy. After the meeting we will send a full recap document that includes all key discussion points ranked solution ideas assigned action items and next step timelines within 24 business hours. The recap will also include a link to the meeting recording and slide deck for anyone who wants to review the content or share it with their extended teams.

If you have any questions about the meeting agenda pre work or logistics please reach out to the User Experience Program Manager directly via Slack or email before the end of this week. We will respond to all inquiries within 24 business hours. We are excited to collaborate with all of you to build a better experience for our users and drive meaningful results for our team in Q3.

Best Regards
The User Experience Strategy Team

there’s a common, lazy take that frames 2010’s the social network as “the facebook movie,” a disposable biopic about a random tech startup that blew up. that take could not be more wrong. directed by david fincher, written by aaron sorkin, and adapted from ben mezrich’s nonfiction book the accidental billionaires, the film is less a chronicle of a website’s origin and more a tight, bitter, eerily prophetic fable about ambition, class alienation, and the empty cost of chasing acceptance in spaces that were never built to let you in.

the film opens in a dim, noisy harvard bar, where 19-year-old mark zuckerberg, played with jittery, razor-sharp awkwardness by jesse eisenberg, is on a date with his girlfriend erica albright. the dialogue is pure sorkin: rapid-fire, layered, equal parts witty and cruel, as mark rants about his obsession with getting into the school’s elite, exclusive final clubs, sniping at erica for going to a lesser school, and dismissing her concerns in favor of his own desperate need to prove he’s worthy of the upper crust. by the end of the scene, erica dumps him, telling him he’ll go through life thinking girls don’t like him because he’s a nerd, when really it’s because he’s an asshole. that one petty, personal rejection, not some grand vision of global connection, is the spark that sets the entire story in motion. mark goes back to his dorm, gets drunk, hacks all of harvard’s dorm directories to build facemash, a crude site that lets students rank female classmates by attractiveness, and in the process draws the attention of both the wealthy winklevoss twins and their business partner divya narendra, who hire him to build their exclusive harvard dating site, and his only real friend eduardo saverin, a well-off but similarly ostracized classmate who puts up $1,000 to fund mark’s new idea, “the facebook.”

sorkin’s script leans into a dual deposition framing device, cutting between the site’s chaotic 2003 and 2004 origins and two parallel lawsuits filed against mark years later: one by the winklevosses and narendra, who claim he stole their idea, and one by eduardo, who was pushed out of the company and cheated out of his shares once the site took off. the framing works perfectly because it rejects any pretense of objective truth. every character’s version of events is colored by their hurt, their greed, their own unmet desires. the winklevosses, old money legacy kids who’ve never had to work for anything in their lives, frame mark as a thief who stole their shot at success, but mark’s sharp retort — “if you guys were the inventors of facebook, you’d have invented facebook” — lands because it’s true: they had the idea for an exclusive, elite social space, but mark had the vision to turn it into something for everyone, or at least everyone who wanted to perform a polished version of their life for peers.

the performances are uniformly perfect. eisenberg never plays mark as a one-note villain or a heroic genius; he’s a deeply insecure, socially stunted kid who can’t hold a normal conversation, can’t read social cues, and can’t stop lashing out at the people who care about him because he’s convinced everyone is secretly looking down on him. andrew garfield turns eduardo into the film’s beating heart, a loyal friend who just wanted to build something with the only person who ever got him, only to be cast aside the second mark meets someone cooler: sean parker, the co-founder of napster, played with chaotic, charismatic charm by justin timberlake. sean is everything mark wants to be: suave, famous, embedded in silicon valley’s cool crowd, convinced the facebook can be a billion-dollar global empire, not just a fun college site. timberlake plays him as equal parts visionary and grifter, a guy who talks a big game but is just as desperate to prove he’s not a washed-up has-been as mark is to prove he’s not a random nerd from new york.

fincher’s direction is as precise and cold as mark’s code. the harvard scenes are shot in muted grays and deep browns, the crisp, stuffy halls of the final clubs feeling like fortresses that lock mark out, while the later silicon valley scenes are brighter but sterile, all white walls and open floor plans that feel empty even when they’re packed with interns and party guests. the score, by trent reznor and atticus ross, is one of the best film scores of the 21st century, a pulsing, glitchy electronic tapestry that captures both the giddy high of building something new and the quiet, gnawing paranoia of watching it fall apart. the way the score distorts and warps during the henley royal regatta scene, where the winklevoss twins row a race against a dutch team, is masterful: the old, genteel world of elite rowing and old money feels slow, outdated, being left behind by the fast, messy, unregulated tech world mark is building.

the film is not without its critics, many of whom point out the large liberties it takes with the real story of facebook’s founding: erica albright is a composite character, mark zuckerberg was already dating his future wife priscilla chan when the site launched, and many of the more dramatic moments of betrayal are exaggerated for effect. but those criticisms miss the point. the social network is not a documentary, it’s a myth, a story about what it means to build a tool meant to connect people when you can barely connect to anyone yourself. when the film came out in 2010, facebook was still mostly used by college students, a fun way to share party photos and poke crushes, and the film felt like a snappy, clever drama about a startup success story. now, more than a decade later, as we grapple with the damage social media has done to privacy, democracy, and real human connection, the film feels almost prophetic. mark’s core flaw — his complete disinterest in the human cost of the thing he built, his willingness to cast aside friends and ethics to grow his empire — is exactly the flaw that led to facebook’s decades of scandals, from cambridge analytica to the spread of misinformation to the platform’s role in radicalizing people across the globe.

the final shot of the film is one of the most haunting endings in recent cinema. after settling both lawsuits for undisclosed sums, mark sits alone in a conference room, his lawyers packing up around him, the youngest billionaire in the world. he pulls up facebook on his laptop, navigates to erica’s profile, and clicks “add friend.” then he sits there, refreshing the page over and over, waiting for a response. he built the largest social network in human history, a platform that connects billions of people across the world, but he’s still the same lonely, rejected kid sitting in his dorm room, desperate for someone to notice him, desperate to be accepted by the people who never wanted him. there’s no triumphant speech, no happy ending, no grand moment of victory. just a guy with all the money and power in the world, sitting alone, refreshing a screen.

the social network works because it never moralizes about social media, never tells you facebook is good or bad. it just shows you the broken, lonely kid who built it, the friends he hurt along the way, and the empty, hollow success that came out of one petty, drunk night after a bad date. it’s one of the best films of the 2010s, a movie that only gets better and more relevant the longer we live in the world it predicted.

ਇਹ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਪੱਟੀ ਦਾ ਉਦੇਸ਼ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਇੰਜੀਨੀਅਰਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਹੁਨਰਾਂ ਦਾ ਨਿਰਪੱਖ, ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ-ਆਧਾਰਿਤ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਕਰਨਾ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਨਿਯੁਕਤੀ, ਤਰੱਕੀ, ਕਾਰਜਕੁਸ਼ਲਤਾ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਸਿਖਲਾਈ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਦਾ ਪਤਾ ਲਗਾਉਣ ਲਈ ਵਰਤੀ ਜਾ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ।

---

## ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਦੇ ਪੱਧਰ
ਹਰੇਕ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਖੇਤਰ ਦਾ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਹੇਠ ਲਿਖੇ 4 ਪੱਧਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ:
1. **ਪੱਧਰ 1: ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤੀ** (0-2 ਸਾਲ ਅਨੁਭਵ) – ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਹੁਨਰ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ, ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ
2. **ਪੱਧਰ 2: ਮੱਧਮ** (2-5 ਸਾਲ ਅਨੁਭਵ) – ਸੁਤੰਤਰ ਕੰਮ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਆਮ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਲ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ
3. **ਪੱਧਰ 3: ਵਰਿਸ਼ਠ** (5-10 ਸਾਲ ਅਨੁਭਵ) – ਵੱਡੇ ਪ੍ਰਾਜੈਕਟਾਂ ਦਾ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਨੇਤ੍ਰਿਤਵ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਟੀਮ ਦਾ ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ
4. **ਪੱਧਰ 4: ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਕ** (10+ ਸਾਲ ਅਨੁਭਵ) – ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਲਈ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਨੀਤੀਆਂ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਉੱਚਤਮ ਪੱਧਰ ਦੀ ਮਾਹਰੀ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ

---

## ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਖੇਤਰ ਅਤੇ ਪੱਧਰ-ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਵਰਣਨ
ਹਰੇਕ ਖੇਤਰ ਨੂੰ 1 ਤੋਂ 4 ਤੱਕ ਸਕੋਰ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਹੇਠ ਲਿਖੇ ਮਾਪਦੰਡਾਂ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ:

### 1. ਸੰਕੇਤ ਲਿਪੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਣਵੱਤਾ
| ਪੱਧਰ | ਵਰਣਨ |
|------|--------|
| 1 | ਸਧਾਰਣ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਲਈ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਸੰਕੇਤ ਲਿਪੀ ਲਿਖ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਆਪਣੀ ਲਿਪੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਆਮ ਗਲਤੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਖੋਜ ਕੇ ਠੀਕ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਟੀਮ ਦੇ ਲਿਪੀ ਸਟਾਈਲ ਨਿਯਮਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਫਾਲੋ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਛੋਟੇ ਇਕਾਈ ਪਰੀਕਸ਼ਣ ਲਿਖ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| 2 | ਜਟਿਲ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਲਈ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ ਬਣਾ ਕੇ ਕੁਸ਼ਲਤਾ ਨਾਲ ਲਿਪੀ ਲਿਖ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਲਿਪੀ ਦੀ ਗੁਣਵੱਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਬਿਹਤਰ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਮੁੜ-ਰਚਨਾ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਦੂਜਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਲਿਪੀ ਦੀ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਕਰ ਕੇ ਕਮੀਆਂ ਪਛਾਣ ਕੇ ਸੁਝਾਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਮਾਂ ਸੀਮਾ ਅੰਦਰ ਗੁਣਵੱਤਾਪੂਰਨ ਕੰਮ ਪੂਰਾ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| 3 | ਪੂਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝ ਕੇ ਅਧਿਕਾਰਤ, ਸੁਰੱਖਿਅਤ ਅਤੇ ਮੁੜ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਯੋਗ ਲਿਪੀ ਦਾ ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਵੱਡੇ ਪੱਧਰ 'ਤੇ ਪੁਰਾਣੀ ਲਿਪੀ ਬੇਸ ਦੀ ਮੁੜ-ਰਚਨਾ ਦੀ ਯੋਜਨਾ ਬਣਾ ਕੇ ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਟੀਮ ਲਈ ਲਿਪੀ ਗੁਣਵੱਤਾ ਦੇ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਅਤੇ ਸਟਾਈਲ ਗਾਈਡ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| 4 | ਪੂਰੇ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਲਈ ਲਿਪੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਦੀਆਂ ਦੂਰ-ਮਿਆਦੀ ਨੀਤੀਆਂ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਜਟਿਲ ਲਿਪੀ ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਤੁਰੰਤ ਪਛਾਣ ਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਦਾ ਰਾਸਤਾ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ। ਲਿਪੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਦੀਆਂ ਬਿਹਤਰ ਪ੍ਰਥਾਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਫੈਲਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। |

---

### 2. ਮੌਲਿਕ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਮਝ
(ਪਦ੍ਵਰਤੀ, ਅੰਕੜਾ ਸੰਰਚਨਾਵਾਂ, ਕਾਰਜ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ, ਸੰਪਰਕ ਜਾਲ, ਅੰਕੜਾ ਭੰਡਾਰ ਸ਼ਾਮਲ)
| ਪੱਧਰ | ਵਰਣਨ |
|------|--------|
| 1 | ਸਧਾਰਣ ਪਦ੍ਵਰਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਕੜਾ ਸੰਰਚਨਾਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ, ਆਮ ਕੰਮਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਕਾਰਜ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ, ਸੰਪਰਕ ਜਾਲ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਨਿਯਮਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਹੈ। ਅੰਕੜਾ ਭੰਡਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਧਾਰਣ ਪੁੱਛਗਿੱਛ ਲਿਖ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| 2 | ਜਟਿਲ ਪਦ੍ਵਰਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਕੜਾ ਸੰਰਚਨਾਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਚੰਗੀ ਸਮਝ ਹੈ, ਵੱਡੀਆਂ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਹੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਕਾਰਜ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੇ ਜਟਿਲ ਹਿੱਸਿਆਂ (ਪ੍ਰਕਿਰਿਆ, ਮੈਮੋਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਬੰਧਨ) ਦੀਆਂ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਲ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਅੰਕੜਾ ਭੰਡਾਰ ਦੀ ਪੁੱਛਗਿੱਛ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਨੂੰ ਅਨੁਕੂਲ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| 3 | ਸਾਰੇ ਮੌਲਿਕ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਡੂੰਘੀ ਸਮਝ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ, ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਜਟਿਲ ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਕਰਕੇ ਕੁਸ਼ਲਤਾ ਨਾਲ ਹੱਲ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਨਵੇਂ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਖੋਜ ਕਰਕੇ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦੇ ਫਾਇਦੇ-ਨੁਕਸਾਨ ਦਾ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਕਰਕੇ ਟੀਮ ਲਈ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਠੀਕ ਵਿਕਲਪ ਚੁਣਦਾ ਹੈ। ਟੀਮ ਨੂੰ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਿਹਾਰਕ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਬਾਰੇ ਸਿਖਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| 4 | ਸਾਰੇ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਮਾਹਰੀ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ, ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਅਸੰਭਵ ਜਾਪਦੀ ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਦਾ ਰਾਸਤਾ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ। ਪੂਰੇ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਲਈ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਦੇ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਉਦਯੋਗ ਦੇ ਨਵੇਂ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਨਿਗਰਾਨੀ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਨੂੰ ਅੱਗੇ ਵਧਣ ਲਈ ਸੁਝਾਅ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ। |

---

### 3. ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਢਾਂਚਾ ਅਤੇ ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ
| ਪੱਧਰ | ਵਰਣਨ |
|------|--------|
| 1 | ਦਿੱਤੇ ਹੋਏ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਅਤੇ ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਉਸ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਆਪਣਾ ਕੰਮ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਛੋਟੇ ਫੀਚਰਾਂ ਲਈ ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ ਬਣਾਉਣ ਵਿੱਚ ਦੂਜਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਮਦਦ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| 2 | ਮੱਧਮ ਪੱਧਰ ਦੀਆਂ ਫੀਚਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਸੇਵਾਵਾਂ ਲਈ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਅਤ, ਕੁਸ਼ਲ ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ ਬਣਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਮੌਜੂਦਾ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਦੀਆਂ ਕਮੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਛਾਣ ਕੇ ਸੁਝਾਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ ਦਸਤਾਵੇਜ਼ ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਤਰੀਕੇ ਨਾਲ ਬਣਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| 3 | ਪੂਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਜਾਂ ਵੱਡੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਲਈ ਮਜ਼ਬੂਤ, ਅਨੁਕੂਲਨਯੋਗ, ਸੁਰੱਖਿਅਤ ਢਾਂਚਾ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਢਾਂਚੇ ਦੇ ਫੈਸਲਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਨੇਤ੍ਰਿਤਵ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਵਿਕਲਪਾਂ ਦਾ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਕਰਕੇ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਠੀਕ ਫੈਸਲਾ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਮੌਜੂਦਾ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਨੂੰ ਬਿਹਤਰ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਵੱਡੀਆਂ ਯੋਜਨਾਵਾਂ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| 4 | ਪੂਰੇ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਲਈ ਦੂਰ-ਮਿਆਦੀ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਢਾਂਚਾ ਦੀ ਨੀਤੀ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਜਟਿਲ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਦੀ ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਤੁਰੰਤ ਪਛਾਣ ਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਦਾ ਰਾਸਤਾ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ। ਉਦਯੋਗ ਦੇ ਨਵੇਂ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਦੇ ਢੰਗਾਂ ਦੀ ਖੋਜ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਲਈ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਠੀਕ ਵਿਕਲਪ ਚੁਣਦਾ ਹੈ। |

---

### 4. ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਹੱਲ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਪੁੰਨਤਾ
| ਪੱਧਰ | ਵਰਣਨ |
|------|--------|
| 1 | ਆਮ, ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਹੱਲ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਆਪਣੀ ਸੰਕੇਤ ਲਿਪੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਮ ਗਲਤੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਖੋਜ ਕੇ ਠੀਕ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਨਿਪੁੰਨਤਾ ਦੇ ਆਮ ਸਾਧਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਕਰਨਾ ਜਾਣਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| 2 | ਜਟਿਲ, ਅਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਪਛਾਣ ਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਪੂਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਗਲਤੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਤੇਜ਼ੀ ਨਾਲ ਖੋਜ ਕੇ ਠੀਕ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਛੋਟੇ ਹਿੱਸਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੰਡ ਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਦਾ ਤਰੀਕਾ ਅਪਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| 3 | ਬਹੁਤ ਜਟਿਲ, ਲੰਬੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਤੋਂ ਚਲ ਰਹੀਆਂ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਡੂੰਘਾਈ ਨਾਲ ਜਾਂਚ ਕਰਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਟੀਮ ਨੂੰ ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਫਿਰ ਨਾ ਆਏ, ਇਸ ਲਈ ਰੋਕਥਾਮ ਦੇ ਉਪਾਇ ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। |
| 4 | ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਅਸੰਭਵ ਜਾਪਦੀ ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਤੁਰੰਤ ਪਛਾਣ ਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਦਾ ਰਾਸਤਾ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਉਣ ਵਾਲੀਆਂ ਵੱਡੀਆਂ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਹੱਲ ਦਾ ਨੇਤ੍ਰਿਤਵ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਆਵਰਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਰੋਕਣ ਲਈ ਪ੍ਰਕਿਰਿਆਵਾਂ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। |

---

### 5. ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਅਨੁਕੂਲਨ

- ਲਿਪੀ ਦੀ ਗੁਣਵੱਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਬਿਹਤਰ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਮੁੜ-ਰਚਨਾ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਬੇਕਾਰ ਦੀ ਲਿਪੀ ਨੂੰ ਹਟਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਦੂਜਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਲਿਪੀ ਦੀ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਕਰ ਕੇ ਗਲਤੀਆਂ, ਗੁਣਵੱਤਾ ਦੀਆਂ ਕਮੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਛਾਣ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਝਾਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਪੂਰੀ ਫੀਚਰ ਲਈ ਪਰੀਕਸ਼ਣ ਲਿਖ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਏਜ ਟੀ? Wait no, ਏਜ ਟੀ is English, replace with "ਖੁਦ ਕੀਤੀ ਲਿਪੀ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਪਰੀਕਸ਼ਣ ਕਰ ਕੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਨੁਕਸ ਨੂੰ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਹੀ ਠੀਕ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਵਾਪਸੀ ਦੀ ਗੁਣਵੱਤਾ ਠੀਕ ਰੱਖਦੇ ਹੋਏ ਸਮਾਂ ਸੀਮਾ ਅੰਦਰ ਕੰਮ ਪੂਰਾ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।

Great. Now ਪੱਧਰ 3 (ਵਰਿਸ਼ਠ, 5-10 ਸਾਲ):
- ਪੂਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝ ਕੇ ਅਧਿਕਾਰਤ, ਸੁਰੱਖਿਅਤ ਅਤੇ ਮੁੜ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਯੋਗ ਸੰਕੇਤ ਲਿਪੀ ਦਾ ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਪੁਰਾਣੀ, ਜਟਿਲ ਲਿਪੀ ਬੇਸ ਦੀਆਂ ਵੱਡੀਆਂ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਵੱਡੇ ਪੱਧਰ 'ਤੇ ਮੁੜ-ਰਚਨਾ ਦੀ ਯੋਜਨਾ ਬਣਾ ਕੇ ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਟੀਮ ਦੀਆਂ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਲਿਪੀ ਸਮੀਖਿਆਵਾਂ ਦਾ ਨੇਤ੍ਰਿਤਵ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਗੁਣਵੱਤਾ ਦੇ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਟੀਮ ਨੂੰ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਫਾਲੋ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਪ੍ਰੇਰਿਤ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਪਰੀਕਸ਼ਣ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਕਵਰੇਜ? No, ਕਵਰੇਜ is loanword, "ਪਰੀਕਸ਼ਣ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਲਗਾਤਾਰਤਾ" – ਪਰੀਕਸ਼ਣ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਲਗਾਤਾਰਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਯੋਜਨਾਬੱਧ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰੀਕਸ਼ਣ ਦੇ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਲਿਪੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਦੇ ਨਿਯਮ, ਸਟਾਈਲ ਗਾਈਡ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਪੂਰੇ ਟੀਮ ਜਾਂ ਵਿਭਾਗ ਲਈ ਲਾਗੂ ਹੁੰਦੇ ਹਨ।

Perfect. Now ਪੱਧਰ 4 (ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਕ, 10+ ਸਾਲ):
- ਪੂਰੇ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਦੀ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਲੋੜਾਂ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਸੰਕੇਤ ਲਿਪੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਦੇ ਦੂਰ-ਮਿਆਦੀ ਨੀਤੀਆਂ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਜਟਿਲ ਲਿਪੀ ਬੇਸ ਦੀ ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਤੁਰੰਤ ਪਛਾਣ ਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਦਾ ਰਾਸਤਾ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ, ਨਵੀਂ ਤਕਨੀਕਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਲਿਪੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਪੂਰੇ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਲਿਪੀ ਗੁਣਵੱਤਾ ਦੇ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਸਥਾਪਿਤ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਨਿਗਰਾਨੀ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਬਿਹਤਰੀ ਲਈ ਸਮੇਂ-ਸਮੇਂ 'ਤੇ ਸੰਸਕਾਰਨ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਲਿਪੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਦੀਆਂ ਬਿਹਤਰ ਪ੍ਰਥਾਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਫੈਲਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਨਵੇਂ ਇੰਜੀਨੀਅਰਾਂ ਲਈ ਸਿਖਲਾਈ ਦਾ ਸਮੱਗਰੀ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

Great, that's the first competency. Now second competency: ਮੌਲਿਕ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਮਝ (Core Technical Concepts Understanding). Subpoints here are ਪਦ੍ਵਰਤੀ (algorithms), ਅੰਕੜਾ ਸੰਰਚਨਾਵਾਂ (data structures), ਕਾਰਜ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ (OS), ਸੰਪਰਕ ਜਾਲ (networks), ਅੰਕੜਾ ਭੰਡਾਰ (databases).

Now level descriptors for this:

ਪੱਧਰ 1 (ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤੀ):
- ਸਧਾਰਣ ਪਦ੍ਵਰਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਕੜਾ ਸੰਰਚਨਾਵਾਂ (ਜਿਵੇਂ ਕਿ ਸੂਚੀ, ਸਟੈਕ, ਕਿਊ, ਸਾਜ਼ੋ-ਸਾਮਾਨ ਦੀ ਕ੍ਰਮਵਾਰ, ਬਾਈਨਰੀ ਖੋਜ) ਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਆਮ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਕਾਰਜ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਹਿੱਸਿਆਂ (ਪ੍ਰਕਿਰਿਆ, ਮੈਮੋਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਬੰਧਨ) ਦੀ ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸੰਪਰਕ ਜਾਲ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ (TCP/IP, HTTP) ਦੀ ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਹੈ, ਅੰਕੜਾ ਭੰਡਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਧਾਰਣ ਪੁੱਛਗਿੱਛ ਲਿਖ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਜਟਿਲ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਲਈ ਦੂਜਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਮਦਦ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

Wait wait, TCP/IP and HTTP are English, oh right! Replace them with Punjabi descriptions? Wait no, what's the Punjabi term for HTTP? Wait no, maybe describe them: "ਵੈਬ ਸੰਪਰਕ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਪ੍ਰੋਟੋਕੋਲ" no, ਪ੍ਰੋਟੋਕੋਲ is loanword, "ਵੈਬ ਸੰਪਰਕ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਨਿਯਮ" yes! And TCP/IP can be "ਅੰਤਰਜਾਲ ਸੰਪਰਕ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਨਿਯਮ ਸਮੂਹ" perfect, no English terms. Let's adjust that line: "ਸੰਪਰਕ ਜਾਲ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ (ਅੰਤਰਜਾਲ ਸੰਪਰਕ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਨਿਯਮ ਸਮੂਹ, ਵੈਬ ਸੰਪਰਕ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਨਿਯਮ) ਦੀ ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਹੈ, ਅੰਕੜਾ ਭੰਡਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਧਾਰਣ ਪੁੱਛਗਿੱਛ ਲਿਖ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।" Great, no English now.

Now ਪੱਧਰ 2 (ਮੱਧਮ):
- ਜਟਿਲ ਪਦ੍ਵਰਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਕੜਾ ਸੰਰਚਨਾਵਾਂ (ਗਰਾਫ, ਟਰਾਈ, ਡਾਈਨਾਮਿਕ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮਿੰਗ? No, wait ਡਾਈਨਾਮਿਕ ਪ੍ਰੋਗਰਾਮਿੰਗ is English, replace with "ਗਤਿਸ਼ੀਲ ਪਦ੍ਵਰਤੀ ਢਾਂਚਾ" yes, ਅਤੇ ਸੌਰਟਿੰਗ ਐਲਗੋਰਿਦਮ no, "ਕ੍ਰਮਬੱਧ ਕਰਨ ਦੇ ਜਟਿਲ ਪਦ੍ਵਰਤੀ") ਦੀ ਚੰਗੀ ਸਮਝ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਵੱਡੀਆਂ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਹੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਕਾਰਜ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੇ ਜਟਿਲ ਹਿੱਸਿਆਂ (ਥ੍ਰੈੱਡਿੰਗ, ਲੌਕਿੰਗ, ਮੈਮੋਰੀ ਲੀਕ) ਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜੀਆਂ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਲ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸੰਪਰਕ ਜਾਲ ਦੇ ਜਟਿਲ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਹੈ, ਅੰਕੜਾ ਭੰਡਾਰ ਦੀ ਅਨੁਕੂਲਨ, ਸੰਰਚਨਾ, ਅਤੇ ਪੁੱਛਗਿੱਛ ਦੀ ਗਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਬਿਹਤਰ ਕਰਨ ਦਾ ਤਰੀਕਾ ਜਾਣਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਨਵੇਂ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਸਿੱਖ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਕੰਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।

Perfect, no English here. Now ਪੱਧਰ 3 (ਵਰਿਸ਼ਠ):
- ਸਾਰੇ ਮੌਲਿਕ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਡੂੰਘੀ ਸਮਝ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ, ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਜਟਿਲ ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਕਰਕੇ ਕੁਸ਼ਲਤਾ ਨਾਲ ਹੱਲ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਨਵੀਆਂ ਤਕਨੀਕਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਨਵੇਂ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਖੋਜ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਫਾਇਦੇ-ਨੁਕਸਾਨ ਦਾ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਕਰਕੇ ਟੀਮ ਲਈ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਠੀਕ ਵਿਕਲਪ ਚੁਣਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਅੰਕੜਾ ਭੰਡਾਰ, ਸੰਪਰਕ ਜਾਲ, ਕਾਰਜ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੇ ਜਟਿਲ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਟੀਮ ਦਾ ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਵਿਹਾਰਕ ਜ਼ਰੂਰਤਾਂ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰਨ ਦੇ ਤਰੀਕੇ ਬਾਰੇ ਟੀਮ ਨੂੰ ਸਿਖਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

Great. Now ਪੱਧਰ 4 (ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਕ):
- ਸਾਰੇ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਮਾਹਰੀ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ, ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਅਸੰਭਵ ਜਾਪਦੀ ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਹੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਕਰਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਦਾ ਰਾਸਤਾ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਪੂਰੇ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਲਈ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਦੇ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਨਵੀਆਂ ਤਕਨੀਕਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਅਪਣਾਉਣ ਦੀ ਨੀਤੀ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਉਦਯੋਗ ਦੇ ਨਵੇਂ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਤਕਨੀਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਨਿਗਰਾਨੀ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਨੂੰ ਅੱਗੇ ਵਧਣ ਲਈ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਅਪਣਾਉਣ ਦਾ ਸੁਝਾਅ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਮੌਲਿਕ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਬਾਰੇ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਿਖਲਾਈ ਕੰਮਕਾਜ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

Third competency: ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਢਾਂਚਾ ਅਤੇ ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ (Technical Architecture and Design). Let's do level descriptors here.

ਪੱਧਰ 1 (ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤੀ):
- ਦਿੱਤੇ ਹੋਏ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਅਤੇ ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਉਸ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਆਪਣਾ ਕੰਮ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਛੋਟੇ ਫੀਚਰਾਂ ਲਈ ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ ਬਣਾਉਣ ਵਿੱਚ ਦੂਜਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਮਦਦ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਢਾਂਚੇ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਹਿੱਸਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਪੱਧਰ 2 (ਮੱਧਮ):
- ਮੱਧਮ ਪੱਧਰ ਦੀਆਂ ਫੀਚਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਸੇਵਾਵਾਂ ਲਈ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਅਤ, ਕੁਸ਼ਲ ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ ਬਣਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਮੌਜੂਦਾ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਦੀਆਂ ਕਮੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਛਾਣ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਝਾਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਵੱਡੇ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਦੇ ਫੈਸਲਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਭਾਗ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਆਪਣੇ ਵਿਚਾਰ ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਰੱਖ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ ਦਸਤਾਵੇਜ਼ ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਤਰੀਕੇ ਨਾਲ ਬਣਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਪੱਧਰ 3 (ਵਰਿਸ਼ਠ):
- ਪੂਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਜਾਂ ਵੱਡੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਲਈ ਮਜ਼ਬੂਤ, ਅਨੁਕੂਲਨਯੋਗ, ਸੁਰੱਖਿਅਤ ਢਾਂਚਾ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਢਾਂਚੇ ਦੇ ਫੈਸਲਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਨੇਤ੍ਰਿਤਵ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਵਿਕਲਪਾਂ ਦੇ ਫਾਇਦੇ-ਨੁਕਸਾਨ ਦਾ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਕਰਕੇ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਠੀਕ ਫੈਸਲਾ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਮੌਜੂਦਾ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਨੂੰ ਬਿਹਤਰ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਵੱਡੀਆਂ ਯੋਜਨਾਵਾਂ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਢਾਂਚੇ ਦੇ ਦਸਤਾਵੇਜ਼ ਬਣਾਉਣ ਦੇ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਟੀਮ ਨੂੰ ਰੂਪਰੇਖਾ ਬਣਾਉਣ ਲਈ ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਪੱਧਰ 4 (ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਕ):
- ਪੂਰੇ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਲਈ ਦੂਰ-ਮਿਆਦੀ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਢਾਂਚਾ ਦੀ ਨੀਤੀ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਦੇ ਵਿਕਾਸ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਨੂੰ ਪੂਰਾ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਨੂੰ ਅਨੁਕੂਲ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਜਟਿਲ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਦੀ ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਤੁਰੰਤ ਪਛਾਣ ਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਦਾ ਰਾਸਤਾ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ, ਵੱਡੇ-ਪੱਧਰ ਦੇ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਬਦਲਾਅ ਦੀ ਯੋਜਨਾ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਉਦਯੋਗ ਦੇ ਨਵੇਂ ਢਾਂਚੇ ਦੇ ਢੰਗਾਂ ਦੀ ਖੋਜ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਲਈ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਠੀਕ ਵਿਕਲਪ ਚੁਣਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਢਾਂਚੇ ਬਾਰੇ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਸਾਂਝ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਨਵੇਂ ਇੰਜੀਨੀਅਰਾਂ ਲਈ ਢਾਂਚਾ ਸਿਖਲਾਈ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਬੰਧ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

Fourth competency: ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਹੱਲ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਪੁੰਨਤਾ (Problem Solving and Debugging). This is core technical skill.

ਪੱਧਰ 1 (ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤੀ):
- ਆਮ, ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਹੱਲ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਆਪਣੀ ਸੰਕੇਤ ਲਿਪੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਮ ਗਲਤੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਖੋਜ ਕੇ ਠੀਕ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਜਟਿਲ ਨਿਪੁੰਨਤਾ ਕੰਮਾਂ ਲਈ ਦੂਜਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਮਦਦ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਆਮ ਟੂਲਸ? No, ਟੂਲਸ is loanword, "ਸਾਧਨ" – ਆਮ ਨਿਪੁੰਨਤਾ ਸਾਧਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਕਰਨਾ ਜਾਣਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਪੱਧਰ 2 (ਮੱਧਮ):
- ਜਟਿਲ, ਅਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਪਛਾਣ ਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਪੂਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਗਲਤੀ ਹੈ, ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਤੇਜ਼ੀ ਨਾਲ ਖੋਜ ਕੇ ਠੀਕ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਛੋਟੇ-ਛੋਟੇ ਹਿੱਸਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੰਡ ਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਦਾ ਤਰੀਕਾ ਅਪਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਨਵੇਂ ਨਿਪੁੰਨਤਾ ਸਾਧਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਿੱਖ ਕੇ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਠੀਕ ਸਾਧਨ ਚੁਣ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਪੱਧਰ 3 (ਵਰਿਸ਼ਠ):
- ਬਹੁਤ ਜਟਿਲ, ਲੰਬੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਤੋਂ ਚਲ ਰਹੀਆਂ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਡੂੰਘਾਈ ਨਾਲ ਜਾਂਚ ਕਰਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਪੂਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੇ ਪੱਧਰ 'ਤੇ ਨਿਪੁੰਨਤਾ ਕੰਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਨੇਤ੍ਰਿਤਵ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਟੀਮ ਨੂੰ ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਫਿਰ ਨਾ ਆਏ, ਇਸ ਲਈ ਰੋਕਥਾਮ ਦੇ ਉਪाय ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਟੀਮ ਲਈ ਨਿਪੁੰਨਤਾ ਦੇ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਅਤੇ ਸਰਗਰਮੀਆਂ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਪੱਧਰ 4 (ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਕ):
- ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਅਸੰਭਵ ਜਾਪਦੀ ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਨੂੰ ਤੁਰੰਤ ਪਛਾਣ ਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਦਾ ਰਾਸਤਾ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਉਣ ਵਾਲੀਆਂ ਵੱਡੀਆਂ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਹੱਲ ਦਾ ਨੇਤ੍ਰਿਤਵ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸਮੱਸਿਆਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਆਵਰਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਰੋਕਣ ਲਈ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਪ੍ਰਕਿਰਿਆਵਾਂ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸਮੱਸਿਆ ਹੱਲ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਪੁੰਨਤਾ ਦੀਆਂ ਬਿਹਤਰ ਪ੍ਰਥਾਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਫੈਲਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

Fifth competency: ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਅਨੁਕੂਲਨ (Security and Performance Optimization). Important technical skill.

ਪੱਧਰ 1 (ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤੀ):
- ਆਮ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਗਲਤੀਆਂ (ਜਿਵੇਂ ਕਿ ਪਾਸਵਰਡ ਨੂੰ ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਲਿਖਣਾ, ਇਨਪੁਟ ਦੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਨਾ ਕਰਨਾ) ਤੋਂ ਬਚਣਾ ਜਾਣਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਆਪਣੀ ਸੰਕੇਤ ਲਿਪੀ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਦੀ ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਸਿਧਾਂਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਪੱਧਰ 2 (ਮੱਧਮ):
- ਆਪਣੀ ਲਿਪੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਦੀਆਂ ਕਮੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਛਾਣ ਕੇ ਠੀਕ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਦੇ ਨਿਯਮਾਂ ਅਨੁਸਾਰ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਲਿਪੀ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਕੜਾ ਭੰਡਾਰ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਨੂੰ ਬਿਹਤਰ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਅਨੁਕੂਲਨ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਦੇ ਆਮ ਸਾਧਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਕਰਨਾ ਜਾਣਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਕਿਸੇ ਨਵੀਂ ਫੀਚਰ ਨੂੰ ਬਣਾਉਂਦੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਨੂੰ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਪੱਧਰ 3 (ਵਰਿਸ਼ਠ):
- ਪੂਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੀ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਦਾ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਕਮੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਛਾਣ ਕੇ ਹੱਲ ਦੀ ਯੋਜਨਾ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਪੂਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਨੂੰ ਮਾਪਦਾ ਹੈ, ਵੱਡੇ ਪੱਧਰ 'ਤੇ ਅਨੁਕੂਲਨ ਕਰਕੇ ਗਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਕਾਫੀ ਬਿਹਤਰ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਟੀਮ ਲਈ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਦੇ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਫਾਲੋ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਪ੍ਰੇਰਿਤ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਦੇ ਹਮਲਿਆਂ ਤੋਂ ਬਚਣ ਲਈ ਰੋਕਥਾਮ ਦੇ ਉਪਾਇ ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਪੱਧਰ 4 (ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਕ):
- ਪੂਰੇ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਦੀ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਨੀਤੀ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਦੀ ਨਿਗਰਾਨੀ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਪ੍ਰਕਿਰਿਆਵਾਂ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਭਰ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਦੇ ਮਾਪਦੰਡ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਦੂਰ-ਮਿਆਦੀ ਅਨੁਕੂਲਨ ਦੀ ਯੋਜਨਾ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਉਦਯੋਗ ਦੇ ਨਵੇਂ ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਖ਼ਤਰਿਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਤਕਨੀਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਨਿਗਰਾਨੀ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਲਈ ਸੁਝਾਅ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਬਾਰੇ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਿਖਲਾਈ ਕੰਮਕਾਜ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

Sixth competency: ਸੰਪੂਰਨ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੁਸੰਧਾਨ (Full System Understanding and Research). For senior levels especially.

ਪੱਧਰ 1 (ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤੀ):
- ਆਪਣੇ ਕੰਮ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜੇ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੇ ਹਿੱਸੇ ਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਨਵੀਂ ਤਕਨੀਕਾਂ ਬਾਰੇ ਜਾਣਨ ਲਈ ਦੂਜਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਮਦਦ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਆਪਣੇ ਕੰਮ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜੀਆਂ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਇਕੱਠੀ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਪੱਧਰ 2 (ਮੱਧਮ):
- ਆਪਣੀ ਟੀਮ ਦੇ ਕੰਮ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੀ ਚੰਗੀ ਸਮਝ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਆਪਣੇ ਕੰਮ ਲਈ ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਨਵੀਂ ਤਕਨੀਕਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਸਿੱਖ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਖੋਜ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਨਵੀਂ ਤਕਨੀਕਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਫਾਇਦੇ-ਨੁਕਸਾਨ ਦਾ ਬੁਨਿਆਦੀ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਪੱਧਰ 3 (ਵਰਿਸ਼ਠ):
- ਪੂਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੀ ਡੂੰਘੀ ਸਮਝ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ, ਵੱਡੇ ਬਦਲਾਅ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਭਾਵ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਨਵੀਆਂ ਤਕਨੀਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਡੂੰਘੀ ਅਨੁਸੰਧਾਨ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਟੀਮ ਲਈ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਠੀਕ ਵਿਕਲਪ ਚੁਣਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਕਮੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਹੀ ਪਛਾਣ ਕੇ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਹੱਲ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਯੋਜਨਾ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

ਪੱਧਰ 4 (ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਕ):
- ਪੂਰੇ ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਦੀਆਂ ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਲੀਆਂ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਸਮਝ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ, ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਬਦਲਾਅ ਦਾ ਸੰਪੂਰਨ ਪ੍ਰਭਾਵ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਉਦਯੋਗ ਦੀ ਨਵੀਂ ਤਕਨੀਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਲਗਾਤਾਰ ਅਨੁਸੰਧਾਨ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸੰਸਥਾਨ ਨੂੰ ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਤੌਰ 'ਤੇ ਅੱਗੇ ਰੱਖਣ ਲਈ ਨੀਤੀਆਂ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
- ਅਨੁਸੰਧਾਨ ਦੇ ਨਤੀਜਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਵਿਹਾਰਕ ਕੰਮਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਲਾਗੂ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਯੋਜਨਾ ਬਣਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਲਾਭ ਦਾ ਮੁਲਾਂਕਣ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

Seventh competency: ਤਕਨੀਕੀ ਸਹਿਯੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਸਾਂਝ (Technical Collaboration and Knowledge Sharing). This is technical because it's about code reviews, technical guidance, etc.

**Linseed Steam & Wild Geese**
November seeps through the storefront’s fogged skin—
espresso hisses, a jazz horn frays at the edges,
the last unclaimed booth wears a crumb of poppyseed muffin
and the faint ghost of someone’s leftover sneeze.
I’m hovering, laptop dead, chapbook slipping
from my coat pocket, when she looks up:
charcoal smudge on her jaw, ukulele case propped
like a half-told secret against the vinyl booth edge.

I ask if the seat’s taken, she says only if you don’t mind
my terrible sketching, holds up a notebook half-full
of barista portraits, rain streaks, a very wonky goose.
I laugh, say I’ve been carrying Mary Oliver’s geese
around in my bag all week, and fumble the chapbook
to prove it, pages fluttering open to the line
you do not have to be good. She leans in, elbows on the table,
says I wrote that on my forearm last Tuesday when I quit my office job.

We split the last lemon poppyseed muffin, argue
about whether oat milk tastes like wet cardboard
(she says yes, I say no, we compromise by stealing sips
of each other’s drinks: her black cold brew bitter as regret,
my lavender latte sweet as a first crush). She shows me sketches
of stray cats from the alley out back, their tails curled
like tiny question marks; I show her photos of the foster puppies
I’m watching, all wiggly bellies and too-big paws.
The barista yells a name neither of us recognizes three times.
No one moves. The rain slows to a drizzle, then stops,
golden hour leaking through the fog like melted honey.

She scribbles her number on a napkin, dots the i
with a tiny charcoal cat, I add a doodle of a floppy-eared puppy
next to it, tuck it into my chapbook like a pressed four-leaf clover.
We hoist our bags, bump shoulders soft as milk froth at the door,
the bell above the jamb jingling loud enough to jolt
the barista from wiping down the chipped ceramic mugs.
She calls after us, half-smiling, already reaching for the next order slip:
Is there anything else I can help with?

hot take of the week: if your squad’s go-to hang is still the same burger joint where the fry cook knows your order by heart, you’re sleeping on Buena Onda, the Argentinian spot that just opened 10 minutes from the mall. I dragged my 4 most chaotic friends there Saturday night fully expecting to leave hungry and bored, and instead I left with a grease stain on my new jeans, a bag of cookies, and a new life goal of marrying the person who makes their empanadas.

*the empanada situation is so unhinged I almost fought my best friend over the last beef one*
Y’all know those sad frozen empanadas your mom microwaves when she’s too tired to make pasta? These are not those. These are Argentinian-style, stuffed to the gills with seasoned ground beef, melty provolone, and little salty olive bits that make your brain do a backflip. We ordered a dozen for the table, and when Mia tried to claim the last beef one saying “ham and cheese is for people who don’t hate joy” I literally put it in my mouth mid-argument to claim squatters rights. Worth it. The grease stain on my jeans is now a badge of honor I will never wash off.

If empanadas aren’t enough for your ravenous post-soccer-practice / 6-hour-TikTok-binge stomach, get the asado fries. They’re piled high with grilled steak, more cheese, more chimichurri, and enough seasoning to make your mom yell about sodium for 20 minutes. I shared an order with Javi and he still had enough leftover to feed his feral 12-year-old brother when he got home. Portions? No notes.

*they give you so much free bread you can skip lunch tomorrow (and possibly the day after)*
Let’s be real, most of us are showing up to restaurants with $12 and a prayer that no one asks us to split the bill evenly. Buena Onda gets broke teens. They drop a basket of warm crusty bread and a bowl of that bright green chimichurri sauce on your table before you even open the menu, and they will refill it as many times as you ask. We got three refills before our appetizers came, and our waiter just laughed and brought extra sauce no questions asked. I’m 90% sure you could show up with $2, order a water, and just eat bread for an hour and no one would side-eye you. Iconic behavior, honestly. Also that chimichurri? I would drink it out of a cup. Don’t test me.

Side note for anyone trying to rizz up a crush: bring them here. It’s way fancier than the mall food court, but not so fancy that you have to pretend you know what “parrilla” means (it’s just the grill, don’t panic). You’ll get +10 rizz points automatically, and if you offer them a bite of your empanada? Game over.

*the alfajores here taste like if a cookie and a cloud had a very fancy, dulce de leche baby*
I used to think dulce de leche was just caramel for people who watch too many travel TikToks. I was an idiot. These classic Argentinian cookies are two buttery, melt-in-your-mouth shortbread slabs sandwiched with so much thick, creamy dulce de leche I almost moaned out loud when I took the first bite. They’re dusted with powdered sugar, so you’ll leave with a white mustache that your friends will take 17 photos of to post on their story, but that’s part of the vibe. I bought a pack of 6 to take to school Monday, and I’m already planning to lie and say I only have 2 left so I don’t have to share with my chemistry lab partner who never brings his own snacks.

Final verdict: skip the overpriced pretzel stand at the mall this weekend. Drag your squad, your crush, your weird cousin who only talks about World Cup highlights—whoever. Just get there early, because I’m already planning on going back Friday and I will be hoarding all the beef empanadas for myself. Don’t say I didn’t warn you.

"# 🛜 From War Games to TikTok Dances: The Wild Hidden History of the Internet That Shapes Your Whole Life

Raise your hand if you did at least three of these before first period today: Scrolled TikTok for 10 minutes while you ate cereal, Snapchatted your bestie to complain about math homework, Googled ‘when did the French Revolution happen’ to cram for a pop quiz, and queued up your new favorite Olivia Rodrigo deep cut on Spotify. If your hand’s up (it is), you owe all that to the internet—and no, it wasn’t invented by Mark Zuckerberg or Charli D’Amelio. It started way before you were born, with a bunch of government nerds and a very dramatic Cold War.

Let’s rewind to 1962: The U.S. military was panicking that a Soviet nuclear attack could take out the entire country’s phone system, leaving them with no way to communicate. Their solution? Build a *decentralized* network—meaning no single central hub that could get blown up. If one line went down, data could bounce around other paths to get to its destination. They called it ARPANET, and it’s the grandparent of the internet you use today.

In 1969, a team at UCLA sent the first ever ARPANET message to a lab at Stanford, 350 miles away. The plan? Type ‘LOGIN.’ They got as far as ‘L’… then ‘O’… then the whole system crashed. Iconic. First internet fail ever, and we’ve all been there (looking at you, the time your essay deleted mid-save before a deadline).

Quick vocab drop that will make you sound smarter than your computer science teacher: The internet and the World Wide Web are *not* the same thing. The internet is the global network of wires, satellites, and servers that connects all our devices—think of it like the entire world’s road system. The web? That’s all the stuff you access on that network: TikTok, Google, your school’s homework portal, all of it. It’s the houses, malls, skate parks, and concert venues built on those roads. The internet existed for 20 years before the web was even invented, by a guy named Tim Berners-Lee in 1989 who just wanted scientists to share research easier. No cap, he didn’t even patent it—he gave it away for free for everyone to use. Legend behavior.

By the 90s, regular people (not just government nerds and college profs) could get internet access at home—if you were willing to deal with dial-up. You know that screeching, static-y sound your parents make fun of? That was the sound of your computer fighting to connect to the internet, and if someone picked up the house phone mid-connection? Booted off immediately. Back then, internet was something you used for an hour after school, not something you carried in your pocket. People made GeoCities sites with neon pink backgrounds and tiled unicorn gifs, chatted in AOL chat rooms with usernames like xXsk8erboi99Xx, and waited 45 minutes to download a single 2-minute NSYNC music video. Wild.

The 2000s is when things got chaotic in the best way. Before then, the web was just stuff you looked at—you couldn’t post your own content unless you knew how to code a whole website. Then Web 2.0 hit: Suddenly you could make a MySpace profile with a custom Fall Out Boy profile song, rank your top 8 friends (so much drama), post a video of your cat on YouTube, or join Facebook (which was originally only for Harvard students, lol). Then 2007 dropped the iPhone, and the internet stopped being a thing you sat down to use at a desktop. It was in your pocket, everywhere you went, all the time.

So how does all this 60s war tech and 90s dial-up chaos affect your life right now? Let’s keep it real—this thing is a double-edged sword, no cap.

First, the good stuff that your parents and grandparents could never even dream of: Community. If you’re a teen in a tiny town who’s into competitive origami, trans masc skate culture, or super niche indie visual novels, you don’t have to be alone anymore. The internet lets you find your people, no matter how weird or specific your thing is. Then there’s power: Teens today organize global climate strikes, protest gun violence, and raise millions for charity all on social media, way faster and louder than any generation before you. You also have access to basically all human knowledge for free, whenever you want it. You can learn how to fix your skateboard truck, teach yourself Python coding, or master calculus tricks without paying for a fancy tutor or a college class. And if you’re a creative? You can post your art, your music, your TikTok skits, and build an audience or even a whole business before you even graduate high school. That’s insane—20 years ago, you’d have to beg a record label or a gallery to even look at your work.

But let’s not pretend it’s all perfect. We all know the bad parts: The FOMO when you see your friends at a party you weren’t invited to on your Snap story. The constant pressure to curate a perfect online life that doesn’t match how you actually feel. The misinformation that spreads like wildfire, from fake celebrity drama to dumb health trends that actually hurt people. The fact that tech companies are collecting so much data on you it’s creepy, and that you can never really ‘log off’ the way people could 20 years ago. It’s exhausting, and it’s okay to admit that.

The coolest thing about the internet, though? It’s still being written. The guys who sent that first broken ‘LO’ message in 1969 had no idea their military project would turn into a place where teens make viral dance trends, organize global movements, and find their chosen family. Tim Berners-Lee gave away the web for free because he wanted it to be for everyone, not just rich companies or governments. Now it’s your turn to shape it.

Next time you post a TikTok, join a Discord for your favorite hobby, or text your friend a meme, take two seconds to appreciate the chaotic, messy, revolutionary history that got you here. And who knows? Maybe 50 years from now, some teen will be writing a blog post about the thing you invented that changed the whole internet.

P.S. If you ever want to troll your parents, play a 10-second clip of dial-up noise at full volume at family dinner. Trust me, the reaction is worth it. ✌️"

When the Tang dynasty held power over China from 618 to 907 CE, its nearly three-century reign was defined by dramatic swings between brutal, society-shaking war and hard-won, transformative peace that cemented the dynasty’s legacy as one of medieval history’s most powerful and cosmopolitan empires.

The dynasty emerged from the devastating civil war that tore apart the short-lived Sui dynasty, as decades of Sui overspending on public works and failed border campaigns left millions dead and dozens of rebel factions vying for control of northern China. But the young dynasty soon faced an existential new war on its northern frontier, as the powerful Eastern Göktürk Khaganate raided border towns, seized livestock, and threatened to capture the Tang capital of Chang’an barely a decade after the dynasty’s founding. This era of steady, widespread peace enabled an unprecedented cultural renaissance: poets like Li Bai and Wang Wei composed verses celebrating the beauty of the Tang landscape, woodblock printing spread literacy to new classes, Chang’an grew into a global city home to Persian merchants, Buddhist monks, Japanese scholars, and Arab envoys, and ordinary families thrived without the constant fear of conscription or looting that had defined generations before. "At the end of the 19th century, references to the ‘Austrian Empire’ largely denoted the Austro-Hungarian Dual Monarchy, a multi-ethnic state restructured by the 1867 Ausgleich (Compromise) that granted near-sovereign status to Hungary (Transleithania) alongside the Austrian-ruled Cisleithania, both under the Habsburg dynasty of Franz Joseph I. Sentiments toward this imperial structure among Croatian and Serbian communities—split across the monarchy’s territories and the independent Kingdom of Serbia, recognized formally at the 1878 Congress of Berlin—were far from monolithic, shaped by regional grievances, political ideology, religious identity, and competing visions of national self-determination. For both groups, however, the dual monarchy’s deliberate privileging of German and Hungarian ruling elites created a growing undercurrent of anti-imperial resentment that would define Balkan politics for decades to come.

Croatian sentiments toward the empire were first and foremost mediated by the 1868 Nagodba (Croatian-Hungarian Settlement), which subordinated the autonomous Kingdom of Croatia-Slavonia to Hungarian authority, ceding control of defense, foreign policy, finance, and language policy to Budapest while granting limited autonomy over local governance and cultural affairs. The resulting Hungarian magyarization campaign— which mandated Hungarian as the language of state administration, secondary education, and judicial proceedings, and restricted the use of Croatian in public life—created a defining fault line in Croatian attitudes toward the broader Habsburg system. For moderate Croatian nationalists grouped in the Independent National Party, the imperial court in Vienna was seen as a pragmatic, if unreliable, counterweight to Hungarian hegemony for much of the 1870s and 1880s. This faction advocated for trialism: a restructuring of the monarchy into three equal constituent states (Austria, Hungary, and a South Slav polity led by Croatia) that would elevate Croats to the same status as Germans and Hungarians. Many trialists retained cautious goodwill toward the Habsburg dynasty, pointing to its centuries-long role as a patron of Croatian cultural institutions and a bulwark against Italian irredentism in Dalmatia (which was governed directly from Vienna as part of Cisleithania) and pan-Serb ambitions that they feared would erase Croatian national identity. This pro-imperial pragmatism was also dominant among the Croatian Catholic hierarchy, particularly conservative clergy who viewed the Catholic Habsburg dynasty as a critical defense against Orthodox Serbian expansion, anti-clerical Hungarian liberalism, and secular socialist organizing. The small but influential Croatian aristocracy, many of whom held senior positions in the imperial army and bureaucracy, were also staunchly pro-Habsburg, seeing the empire as a guarantor of their social privilege and political power.

By the 1890s, however, this pro-imperial sentiment was increasingly overshadowed by disillusionment and radical nationalism, driven by Franz Joseph’s repeated rejection of trialist proposals to avoid alienating the Hungarian ruling class. The most vocal critics of the empire were grouped in the Party of Rights, founded in 1861 by Ante Starčević, who framed Croatian national sovereignty as an inherent historical right that had been betrayed by both the Nagodba and the Habsburg dynasty. Initially open to a trialist compromise, Starčević and his followers concluded by the 1880s that the monarchy was structurally incapable of prioritizing South Slav interests over its German and Hungarian core constituents. A 1895 split in the party produced the radical Pure Party of Rights (Frankists), led by Josip Frank, which rejected all cooperation with imperial or Hungarian authorities, framed the Habsburgs as an occupying power, and demanded full Croatian independence. Anti-imperial sentiment also grew among Croatian working class communities concentrated in Zagreb, Rijeka, and Dalmatian industrial centers, who were drawn to socialist and anarchist movements that rejected the monarchy as a tool of aristocratic and capitalist exploitation. Dalmatian Croats, in particular, held far more hostile attitudes toward Vienna than their counterparts in Croatia-Slavonia: governed directly as part of Cisleithania, they faced both germanization policies that prioritized German as an official language and the favoring of Italian urban elites over Croatian peasants and workers, leaving them with no separate Hungarian authority to channel their grievances against. By the late 1890s, a growing Yugoslavist movement, spearheaded by liberal intellectuals like Bishop Josip Juraj Strossmayer (founder of the Yugoslav Academy of Sciences and Arts in Zagreb), united Croatian and Serb activists in Croatia-Slavonia and Dalmatia around the demand for a unified South Slav state, framing the dual monarchy as a common oppressor that deliberately stoked ethnic division between Croats and Serbs to maintain control.

For Serbian communities, sentiment toward the empire was defined primarily by the ideal of pan-Serb unification, which cast the Habsburg monarchy as the single greatest obstacle to national self-determination. In the independent Kingdom of Serbia, anti-Austrian sentiment was the dominant national mood by the 1890s, fueled by two pivotal events: the 1878 Congress of Berlin, which granted Austria-Hungary the right to occupy and administer Bosnia-Herzegovina (a territory with a large Serb majority that was central to Serbian national mythology, tied to the medieval Serbian Empire and the Kosovo Myth), and the 1881 Secret Convention signed by Serbian ruler Milan Obrenović, which made Serbia a de facto Austrian protectorate by barring it from entering alliances without Habsburg approval and ceding control of Serbian foreign trade and military organization to Vienna. This pro-Austrian policy was fiercely opposed by the populist Radical Party, founded in 1881 by Nikola Pašić, which drew support from Serbia’s peasant majority and urban working class. # Gum Hymn
Dawn bleeds pale gold over grandma’s backyard fence,
and the eucalyptus stands first to catch it,
its bark peeling in soft, translucent curls—
dried honey, sun-bleached ash, the soft brown
of a lullaby’s last line. It sheds its skin like a prayer,
leaving smooth, green-gray underbark tight to the trunk,
polished by wind and the small hands of kids
who’ve climbed its lower branches for seventy years:
my mother, me, now my niece, who tucks leaves
into her overalls pocket like lucky coins.

Crush one between your thumb and forefinger:
that sharp, green hymn spills out, clears the sinuses
and the quiet grief that sticks to your throat
after a bad dream, after a funeral, after a week
of staring at screens until your eyes feel like dust.
The leaves hang vertical, tilted to let sunlight slip past,
so the ground under the canopy is stitched
with pale blue dapples, like someone spilled a jar of sky
through the slats of the porch swing. In spring,
the branches burst with fuzzy white flowers,
each one a tiny star stuffed with nectar,
and later come the gum nuts: woody, ribbed cups,
the size of a thumbtack or a child’s marble,
that fall like tiny gifts when the wind picks up.

I used to string them on fishing line for necklaces,
stack them into fairy houses tucked in the root crooks,
fill them with dandelion fluff and shards of sea glass
I found by the highway. That was the tree’s first gift to me:
small, unmarketable, perfect, the kind of use
that doesn’t turn a profit, doesn’t lower a fever,
just makes a seven-year-old feel rich with magic.

But the old uses run deeper, stitched into the land
long before grandma’s house was built, long before
white settlers brought blue gums from Australia
to line California’s dirt roads. The Bundjalung,
the Yorta Yorta, the hundreds of First Nations
who’ve tended eucalyptus forests for 60,000 years,
knew them first as kin: steeped leaves for fever
and chest pain, bark woven into shelters that bowed
but never broke in cyclone wind, trunks hollowed
by fire and time into canoes that glided over rivers
like a secret. They burned the leaves for ceremonial smoke,
to cleanse a space, to carry prayers to the sky.
The Tongva, whose unceded land this backyard sits on,
mixed eucalyptus sap with sage for cough syrup,
wove the tough young branches into baskets
that held acorns, berries, babies wrapped in rabbit fur.

Grandma learned that from Mrs. Romero, the Tongva elder
who lived down the street, who taught her to make salve
from eucalyptus oil, beeswax, a dash of peppermint,
stored in a chipped ceramic jar on the windowsill
above the sink, thick as molasses, smelling of rain
and clean work. When I had croup at seven,
my lungs tight as a closed fist, grandma rubbed it
into my chest, wrapped me in a faded flannel blanket
printed with sunflowers, and sat me on the porch steps
to breathe the tree’s own breath, thick with menthol,
until my wheezing softened, until I could breathe
deep enough to smell the jasmine from the next yard,
until the fear in my chest melted like butter in the sun.

That’s the thing about eucalyptus: they don’t hoard their gifts.
Bees dive into their flowers to make honey that tastes
like summer thunderstorms and wild mint, the kind
you spread on sourdough toast when you’re under the weather,
a spoonful of tree to warm you from the inside out.
Florists snip their young, blue-gray branches for bouquets,
their leaves soft as lamb’s ear, holding their shape
long after roses have turned to crumpled blush,
long after peonies have shed their last petal.
They tuck them into mason jars on kitchen counters,
into bridal wreaths, into front-door wreaths that smell
like winter and welcome all year round, no watering needed.

Farmers plant them in straight rows along field edges,
their tall trunks like sentinels, blocking the hot desert wind
that would scorch lettuce beds, strawberry rows, young orange trees.
Their wood, dense and golden as wheat, is carved into dining tables
that hold seventy years of Sunday dinners, birthday cakes,
arguments and apologies and quiet I love yous.
It’s cut into fence posts that mark property lines
and hold up tomato vines, that outlast ten winters of rain
and three summers of wildfire. It’s pulped into paper
that holds poems, love letters, report cards, obituaries,
the small, messy stories that make a life.

When wildfires sweep through the hills, they don’t burn to nothing:
their buds hide under thick, fire-resistant bark,
waiting for the heat to crack them open, pushing new green shoots
through blackened trunks before the smoke has even cleared.
They are the first green in a charred landscape,
the first sign that life comes back, that even ash can be a gift.
They drop their leathery leaves to mulch the soil, hold the hillsides
together when the rains come, keep mudslides from burying
the small houses at the base of the canyon.

Last week, I clipped a small branch from the old tree,
tucked it into a mason jar on my apartment windowsill,
300 miles from grandma’s house. When I’m stressed,
when my chest feels tight, when I miss her,
I crush a leaf between my fingers, breathe in
that sharp, green hymn. It doesn’t fix everything.
But it clears the air. It reminds me that beauty
doesn’t have to be useless, that utility doesn’t have to be plain.
Some things are made to be smelled, to be climbed,
to heal the sick, to hold up tomatoes, to make little girls
feel rich with magic, to come back even after the fire
has burned everything else away. Some things are made
to give, and give, and give.

# Product Description Poem Template
For e-commerce listings, social media captions, launch emails, and brand content — adaptable for physical goods (apparel, skincare, home goods, pet gear) and digital products (templates, courses, printables). Fill these in to tailor the template to your product:
| Placeholder | Definition |
|-------------|------------|

| [Hero Functional Benefit] | The core job your product does (e.g., keeps water cold 12 hours, cuts planning time by 60%, stops chapped hands) |
